# Sources for affine demands on planar perfect matchings

**Matching hull.** Lovász studies the lattice generated by incidence vectors of perfect matchings. El Maalouly, Steiner and Wulf use a basis of the matching span over a finite field for parity-constrained matching. For affine tests here, append a coordinate 1 to each matching vector before taking the binary span. A basis tests every affine identity on actual matchings by linearity. [Lovász, *Matching structure and the matching lattice*](https://doi.org/10.1016/0095-8956(87)90021-9) · [El Maalouly, Steiner and Wulf, §4](https://doi.org/10.4230/LIPIcs.ISAAC.2023.28)

**Signed enumeration.** Cimasoni and Reshetikhin express surface dimer partition functions in terms of signed Pfaffians and binary homology classes. For prescribed edge-label parities on a plane graph, the corresponding calculation follows directly from character orthogonality. For each character, multiply each edge weight by its character value and evaluate the Pfaffian with one common planar sign normalization. Average the signed values against the character of the target. This gives the exact count in that parity class. [Cimasoni and Reshetikhin, *Dimers on surface graphs and spin structures. I*, §6](https://www.unige.ch/~cimasoni/spinI.pdf)

**Prescribed even pairs.** Loebl gives an explicit planar precedent. For each of g disjoint pairs of edges, a perfect matching must take both edges or neither. Enumerating those choices and using planar matching enumeration computes the weighted generating function in the stated 2^g polynomial-time bound. The paper also proves an ETH lower bound for decision in its planar setting. [Loebl, *The Precise Complexity of Finding Rainbow Even Matchings*, pp. 1–4](https://kam.mff.cuni.cz/~loebl/clanky/remf.pdf)

**Application to OR demands.** For an edge set D, fit one affine form to value 0 on perfect matchings of G−D and value 1 on each family obtained by forcing one edge of D. Lift each forced-edge family to original edge coordinates before taking its hull. Empty families impose no equations. These tests characterize exactly when the OR agrees with an affine form on every actual matching. Once inconsistent affine targets have been rejected, the Fourier filter uses the rank of the fitted forms on matching differences. Remaining OR demands can be enforced by inclusion–exclusion over edge deletions.

Three earlier repository notes supply reusable parts of this calculation. Paths are relative to the research repository root.

- `research/direct-sat-algebra/block-residue/matching-hull-package.md` constructs the homogenized binary matching span on indexed edges.
- `research/interpolation-point/taylor-cuts/forced-matching-hull-obstruction.md` computes conditional label hulls by forcing an edge and adding back its label.
- `research/interpolation-point/taylor-cuts/adaptive-pfaffian-count.md` combines matching-hull restrictions, Walsh characters, signed Pfaffians and gain histograms.
